correctness.rationale: Facewise intrinsic distance is certified by a continuous piecewise Euclidean norm that is globally 1-Lipschitz and by explicit geodesics inside each developed equilateral rhombus. For radii at most one the four developed rhombi contribute complete circular sectors; for larger radii four exact circular-segment complements supply the remaining CDF. Uniform barycentric integration gives the squared moment, direct differentiation gives the size-four jump in the second derivative, and a uniform polar expansion gives the upper-tail constant. A standalone exact rational unfolding checked 65 simple face sequences, 13 distinct images, and all vertex-nearest-image inequalities; independent numerical quadrature and seeded surface samples corroborated the formulas. No numerical evidence substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: A regular octahedron is a canonical polyhedral metric surface, and the vertex-centered area profile is a natural intrinsic metric-measure invariant. The exact all-threshold distribution has a nonobvious cancellation of the geometric equatorial crossing at radius sqrt(3)/2, a sharp second-derivative phase change at radius one, a closed squared-distance moment, and a universal quadratic tip tail for this fixed geometry. These are distinct from the ambient chord problem and from farthest-point dynamics. The full distribution is useful as a reproducible exact benchmark for source-unfolding and polyhedral wavefront-area algorithms, without requiring a broader theorem.
